# NATS Receiver

The NATS receiver receives metrics, logs, and traces from a [NATS](https://nats.io/) messaging system (Core NATS and JetStream).

## Getting Started

### Minimal Configuration

```yaml
receivers:
  nats:
    endpoint: nats://localhost:4222
```

### Production Configuration

```yaml
receivers:
  nats:
    endpoint: nats://nats.production:4222
    queue_group: "otelcol-nats-cluster"
    auth:
      username: "otel-collector"
      password: "${env:NATS_PASSWORD}"
      credentials_file: "/etc/nats/user.creds"
    tls:
      ca_file: "/etc/ssl/certs/nats-ca.pem"
      cert_file: "/etc/ssl/certs/client-cert.pem"
      key_file: "/etc/ssl/certs/client-key.pem"
      insecure_skip_verify: false
    monitor:
      endpoint: "https://nats.production:8222"
      timeout: 10s
      tls:
        ca_file: "/etc/ssl/certs/nats-ca.pem"
    scrape_interval: 10s
    tapped_subjects:
      - "orders.>"
      - "events.>"
      - "telemetry.>"
```

## Configuration Reference

The following settings are available:

- `endpoint` (default = `nats://localhost:4222`): The NATS connection URL.
- `queue_group` (optional): NATS queue group name. When running multiple Collector instances, setting a queue group load-balances message intake across collectors to prevent duplicate traces and logs.
- `auth` (optional):
  - `username`: Plaintext username.
  - `password`: Password (`configopaque.String`).
  - `token`: Authentication token (`configopaque.String`).
  - `nkey`: User NKey seed (`configopaque.String`).
  - `credentials_file`: Path to a NATS `.creds` user credentials file (JWT + seed).
- `tls` (optional): Standard OpenTelemetry [`configtls.ClientConfig`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/config/configtls/README.md) settings (`ca_file`, `cert_file`, `key_file`, `insecure_skip_verify`, `server_name_override`).
- `monitor` (optional): Standard OpenTelemetry [`confighttp.ClientConfig`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/config/confighttp/README.md) settings (`endpoint`, `timeout`, `tls`, `headers`, `proxy_url`) for NATS HTTP monitoring API scraping (`/varz`, `/jsz`).
- `monitor_url` (optional, default = `""`): Convenience endpoint shorthand for `monitor.endpoint`.
- `scrape_interval` (default = `5s`): Frequency for scraping NATS monitoring metrics.
- `tapped_subjects` (default = `["telemetry.>", "events.>", "orders.>"]`): NATS subjects tapped to generate consumer spans.

## Signals

### Metrics

The receiver periodically scrapes NATS server stats (`/varz`) and JetStream stats (`/jsz`) via the configured `monitor` HTTP endpoint and emits in-memory `pmetric.Metrics`.

For the complete list of emitted metrics, types, units, and attribute dimensions, see [documentation.md](documentation.md).

### Logs

The receiver subscribes to NATS server system and advisory events:
- `$SYS.ACCOUNT.*.CONNECT` / `DISCONNECT`
- `$SYS.SERVER.*.CLIENT.CONNECT` / `DISCONNECT`
- `$JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.>` (Stream & consumer actions, delivery errors)

Advisories are transformed into `plog.Logs` with severity mapping (`INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR`), structured attributes, and semantic domain `nats`.

### Traces

The receiver taps configured `tapped_subjects` and extracts distributed trace context from NATS message headers (`nats.Header`) using W3C TraceContext standards:
- Generates `CONSUMER` spans conforming to OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions for Messaging v1.26+.
- Extracts parent trace ID and span ID via `carrier.HeaderCarrier` without mutating the message.
- Supports ephemeral inbox detection (`messaging.destination.anonymous: true`).
